items.title_en: Taiwan Stock Pre‑Market News: Democrats Win US Midterms, Yongfeng Bank’s New Online Banking System Hacked, Advantech Forecasts Double‑Digit Revenue Growth Next Year
paras:
台股盤前要聞 

1.據《CNBC》4日報導，民主黨在美國期中選舉拿下國會兩院，加上川普表態接受結果，緩解籠罩華爾街的政治不確定性，美股期貨從隔夜大跌轉為強勁上揚，道瓊期貨大漲逾800點。不過，市場擔憂資料中心監管收緊，AI基礎建設相關股票表現承壓。
2. 針對3日發生的異常轉帳事件，永豐銀行4日晚間召開記者會，經調查，確定為外部駭客利用「新網銀交易系統」之供應商安全設定漏洞所致。永豐銀行董事長曹為實與總經理莊銘福親上火線，向受影響客戶及社會大眾鞠躬致歉，並直言「此案雖無損失，但商譽影響甚鉅」。目前永豐銀已將該系統全面下架，並正籌備相關事證，準備向該國外軟體供應商進行法律求償。
3.工業電腦大廠研華(2395-TW)4日召開法說會，公司看好，第四季營收將持穩高檔，並有機會超越第三季再創新高，且從目前訂單能見度來看，明年展望樂觀，預估營收將有高雙位數成長，加上經濟規模效益顯現，獲利增幅高於營收表現將成常態。
4.IC 封測廠矽格(6257-TW)4日公布10月營收為21億元，月、年雙增，續創單月歷史新高，單月營收連4個月突破20億元；矽格表示，隨著、光子積體電路(PIC)及光引擎(Optical Engine)等相關測試技術布局，AI相關產品比重將突破30%。
5.台股4日盤中隨美國期中選舉及美國期貨走弱影響，盤中急挫跌破4萬2千點，高低檔震盪達1,885點，創史上第4大震盪，終場收42,948點，成交量放大1.1兆元。外資今日大舉提款近1,498億元，寫下歷史單日第5大賣超，不僅大賣主動式ETF主動統一升級50(00403A-TW)8.4萬張最多，也大賣元大台灣50(0050-TW)7.7萬張居次，個股部分則是連19賣權王台積電(2330-TW)。

paras_en: According to CNBC on the 4th, the Democratic Party captured both chambers of the US Congress in the midterm elections. With former President Trump saying he accepts the results, political uncertainty on Wall Street eased, and US stock futures rebounded sharply after a steep overnight drop, with Dow futures jumping more than 800 points. However, the market remains wary of tighter data‑center regulation, putting pressure on AI‑infrastructure stocks.

Yongfeng Bank held a press conference on the evening of the 4th regarding the abnormal transfer incident that occurred on the 3rd. The investigation found that an external hacker exploited a security‑setting vulnerability in the supplier of its new online‑banking transaction system. Chairman Cao Weishi and General Manager Zhuang Mingfu personally apologized to affected customers and the public, stating that although no financial loss occurred, the damage to the bank’s reputation was substantial. Yongfeng has now taken the system offline and is gathering evidence to pursue legal compensation against the foreign software supplier.

Advantech (2395‑TW) held a legal‑presentation meeting on the 4th. The company is optimistic that fourth‑quarter revenue will remain at a high level and may surpass the third‑quarter peak, and based on current order visibility, the outlook for next year is positive, with revenue expected to grow at a high double‑digit rate. In addition, economies of scale are beginning to show, so profit growth is expected to outpace revenue growth as a new normal.

Integrated circuit test‑maker Siliconware Precision Industries (6257‑TW) announced October revenue of NT$2.1 billion on the 4th, marking month‑over‑month and year‑over‑year growth and setting a new monthly record for the fourth consecutive month with revenue exceeding NT$2 billion. Siliconware said that with its deployment of photonic integrated circuit (PIC) and optical‑engine testing technologies, AI‑related product share is expected to break the 30% threshold.

During intraday trading on the 4th, the Taiwan stock index fell sharply, breaking the 42,000‑point level as the US midterm results and weakening US futures weighed on sentiment. The index swung a total of 1,885 points, the fourth‑largest intraday swing on record, and closed at 42,948 points with turnover reaching NT$1.1 trillion. Foreign investors withdrew about NT$149.8 billion, marking the fifth‑largest single‑day net sell‑off in history, heavily selling the actively managed ETF Active Unified Upgrade 50 (00403A‑TW) with 84,000 lots, followed by the Yuanta Taiwan 50 (0050‑TW) with 77,000 lots, and in individual stocks, the 19‑strike put options on TSMC (2330‑TW) were the most sold.
Democratic landslide fuels post‑election market rally; Trump accepts defeat as Dow futures surge over 800 points.
Yongfeng cyber‑security incident: “No monetary loss but reputation damaged.” The new online‑banking system has been taken offline and the bank will seek compensation from the foreign supplier.
Advantech earnings briefing: Q4 revenue steadies at NT$30 billion, aiming for a new high; optimistic outlook for next year with high double‑digit growth forecast.
Siliconware reports October revenue of NT$2.1 billion, a new monthly record; AI product share expected to exceed 30%.
Foreign investors dump nearly NT$1.5 trillion, the fifth‑largest net sell‑off on record, slashing active ETFs and selling 19‑strike puts on TSMC.
Electronics “Big Five” revenue: Wistron posted October revenue of NT$79.966 billion, a seasonal high, with server outlook remaining positive.
Telecom “Big Three” earnings: Chunghwa Telecom Q3 net profit NT$12.22 billion, EPS NT$1.57, beating analysts’ forecasts.
Taiwan Mobile acquires Jingcheng, exceeding the 39% minimum acquisition threshold and meeting both achievement conditions.
MediaTek hires former Intel executive vice president to expand its data‑center and AI footprint.
US midterms see a shift in Texas; commentator Tong Zi‑xian says the volatile policy direction fails to win voter support.
Fujian‑Jiao reported third‑quarter after‑tax net profit of NT$2.082 billion, up nearly fourfold year‑over‑year, with EPS of NT$3.41.
G2C+ Alliance adds new member Zhi‑Sheng, which will increase its stake in Vision Automation to 75.06% through a share‑exchange acquisition.

items.title: 未必是美夢！邁威爾收購Lumentum市值蒸發千億美元 巴隆點出特斯拉與SpaceX投資人也該警惕
items.title_en: Not Necessarily a Dream! Marvell’s $100 Billion Market‑Cap Loss After Acquiring Lumentum, Barron Warns Tesla and SpaceX Investors to Be Cautious
paras: 特斯拉(TSLA-US)投資人無不高度期待能與SpaceX(SPCX-US)合併，預期後者將以全股票交易方式溢價收購，進而推升特斯拉股價。但巴隆周刊(Barron’s)認為，在特斯拉投資人準備兌現這筆交易帶來的收益之前，應該先了解邁威爾(Marvell)(MRVL-US)與Lumentum(LITE-US)兩家公司股價發生的事。
邁威爾周一(2日)同意以全股票交易方式收購Lumentum，對後者的估值為每股1,132美元，較10月28日收盤價溢價24%。按照目前交易條件，Lumentum股東每持有1股Lumentum股票，將取得4.5股邁威爾股票。
但消息公布後，當天市場反應冷淡，Lumentum周一重挫近19%，收在每股684.40美元，邁威爾股價也下跌近13%，收在每股171.41美元。
換句話說，邁威爾同意以每股1,132美元收購Lumentum，但截至周一收盤，Lumentum股價已比這個價格低了約40%。邁威爾股價也較10月28日收盤價251.65美元下跌逾30%。
市場顯然非常不看好這筆交易。兩家公司合併後的總市值，已從10月28日約3,300億美元，降至周一的2,300億美元。這筆交易意在整合人工智慧(AI)資料中心擴建潮核心的高階晶片與高階光學連接器製造業務，卻讓兩家公司合計蒸發約1,000億美元市值。
輝達(NVDA-US)執行長黃仁勳6月曾暗示，邁威爾的價值可能達到1兆美元。邁威爾市值以周一收盤價計算約為1,500億美元，股價則比6月創下的52周高點329.88美元下跌近50%。
巴隆指出，通常當投資人看好一筆併購交易時，合併後公司的總價值也會提高，發揮一加一大於二的效果。而當企業價值上升時，投資人可以檢視交易預期創造的綜效金額，並與市值增幅比較，以判斷市場反應是否合理。
這筆交易中，兩家公司預料將創造10億美元綜效，但以合併後市值變化(蒸發1000億美元)計算，綜效倍數為負100倍。
投資人反對這筆交易有幾個原因，包括漫長的監管審查、讓製造商(Lumentum)與晶片設計商(邁威爾)合併的作法不尋常，以及股權稀釋問題。
全股票併購交易並不保證被收購公司的股價會上漲，交易完成後，這些股票的價值將與收購方股價連動。
投資人目前對SpaceX和特斯拉的預期是，SpaceX可能提出20%或30%的溢價，把特斯拉股價推升至500美元
巴隆認為，雖然SpaceX與特斯拉的投資人很可能會大力支持馬斯克打造垂直整合AI公司的願景，但從邁威爾和Lumentum的例子來看，最好還是為合併案宣布後的股價劇烈波動，做好準備。
paras_en: Tesla (TSLA-US) investors are highly期待 (eager) for a merger with SpaceX (SPCX-US), expecting the latter to acquire Tesla in an all‑stock deal at a premium, which would boost Tesla’s share price. However, Barron’s argues that before Tesla investors try to cash in on such a deal, they should first understand what happened to the stock prices of Marvell (MRVL-US) and Lumentum (LITE-US).

On Monday (the 2nd), Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all‑stock transaction, valuing Lumentum at $1,132 per share, a 24% premium to its October 28 closing price. Under the terms, Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 shares of Marvell for each Lumentum share they own.
But market reaction was muted after the announcement; Lumentum plunged nearly 19% on Monday, closing at $684.40 per share, while Marvell’s stock fell about 13% to $171.41.

In other words, Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum at $1,132 per share, yet by Monday’s close Lumentum was trading roughly 40% below that price. Marvell’s own share price was also down more than 30% from its October 28 close of $251.65.

The market clearly dislikes the deal. The combined market value of the two companies fell from about $330 billion on October 28 to $230 billion on Monday. The transaction, intended to combine high‑end chips for AI data‑center expansion with high‑end optical‑connector manufacturing, has erased roughly $100 billion of market value for the two firms.

NVIDIA (NVDA‑US) CEO Jensen Huang hinted in June that Marvell could be worth $1 trillion. Based on Monday’s closing price, Marvell’s market cap is about $150 billion, and its share price is down nearly 50% from the 52‑week high of $329.88 set in June.

Barron notes that when investors are optimistic about an acquisition, the combined company’s total value usually rises, creating a “one‑plus‑one‑greater‑than‑two” effect. When enterprise value climbs, investors can compare the expected synergies with the increase in market cap to judge whether the market’s reaction is reasonable.
In this deal, the two firms expected to generate $1 billion of synergies, but given the post‑merger market‑cap loss of $100 billion, the synergy multiple is negative 100‑times.

Investors oppose the deal for several reasons, including a lengthy regulatory review, the unusual pairing of a manufacturer (Lumentum) with a chip designer (Marvell), and concerns about equity dilution.
An all‑stock acquisition does not guarantee that the target’s share price will rise; after the deal closes, the target’s stock value will move in tandem with the acquirer’s price.
Investors currently expect SpaceX might offer a 20%‑30% premium for Tesla, pushing Tesla’s share price up to $500.

Barron believes that while SpaceX and Tesla investors are likely to strongly support Musk’s vision of a vertically integrated AI company, the Marvell‑Lumentum example suggests they should be prepared for sharp post‑announcement stock volatility.

items.title: 〈美國期中選舉〉選完也別急著追AI股！華爾街提醒贏家輸家要挑清楚
items.title_en: Don't Rush AI Stocks After the U.S. Midterms! Wall Street Says Winners and Losers Must Be Clearly Identified
paras: 民主黨在美國期中選舉拿下國會兩院，美股周三上漲，部分AI概念股卻逆勢走低。華爾街分析師認為，選舉結果可能讓資料中心建設面臨更多限制，但算力需求並未消失；真正的變數在於建設速度、成本，以及放慢投資能否緩解市場對過度舉債的疑慮。
據《彭博》報導，那斯達克100指數上漲逾1%之際，CoreWeave(CRWV-US)、輝達(NVDA-US)及邁威爾(MRVL-US)等AI相關股票下跌。對分析師而言，這場選舉既帶來政策風險，也可能促使產業重新檢視支出紀律。

需求不會消失 資料中心恐蓋得更慢更貴

Truist投資長暨首席市場策略師Keith Lerner認為，選舉增加了資料中心發展路徑與速度的不確定性，但龐大算力需求仍會支持建設。業者可能面臨租稅優惠調整、地方反對，必須改變設廠地點，或接受更多限制與配套條件。
Wealthspire投資長Brad Long指出，德州選舉結果可能讓兩黨政治人物更加重視反資料中心民意。為了爭取連任，更多地方官員可能跟進，主張保護社區免受資料中心擴張影響。
他認為，市場需要消化的問題，不是資料中心會不會蓋，而是「蓋在哪裡、需要多久，以及得通過多少行政程序」。這些阻力可能延後資本支出，也推遲AI投資效益實現的時間。
RWA Wealth Partners投資長JP Powers則認為，市場擔憂可能有些過度，既有計畫未必受到太大影響。不過，業者若須增加地方回饋或因應更多法規，確實可能推升建設與營運成本。

擴張放慢未必全是壞事 有助緩解燒錢壓力

野村跨資產策略師Charlie McElligott提出另一種解讀：選舉若迫使美國資料中心建設放慢，可能緩和大型雲端業者不斷加碼資本支出的競賽，減輕市場對大量發債、股票籌資及自由現金流消耗的疑慮。
這也是選後市場可能偏向樂觀看待的原因之一。在此之前，投資人已開始擔心，AI投資規模持續膨脹，相關融資需求與回報前景是否能夠匹配。
盈透證券首席策略師Steve Sosnick表示，市場對業者支出過於激進、借款規模過大的擔憂有其道理。若建設速度降至較可控的程度，雖然對供應商不利，卻可能替產業帶來市場願意接受的財務紀律。
他也指出，資料中心建設已有龐大動能，牽涉大量就業，幾位州長當選及國會權力更替，不至於讓整體發展完全停下來。

年底行情添阻力 科技股反彈仍須挑選贏家

Miller Tabak首席市場策略師Matt Maley則提醒，AI產業面臨的阻力正在增加，可能讓市場更難出現期中選舉年份常見的年底漲勢。他預期，反對資料中心進駐社區的聲音，也將迅速成為2028年選舉議題。
加拿大皇家銀行資本市場美股策略主管Lori Calvasina認為，即使國會未採取明顯行動，州長選舉結果仍帶來政策風險，因為AI與資料中心已是部分激烈選戰的重要議題。她也對選舉能否成為市場風險解除的轉折點抱持保留態度。
摩根大通(JPM-US)全球市場情報主管Andrew Tyler則維持短線看多科技股的立場。他指出，德州候任州長Gina Hinojosa主張，在新規範建立前立即暫停資料中心建設，但實際影響仍有不同解讀。
一種可能是既有工程與許可繼續推進，新計畫轉往其他州；另一種則是整體建設放慢，帶動資本支出下降。Tyler表示，不會放棄科技股交易，仍看好戰術性反彈，但市場可能更加挑剔科技與AI領域的贏家及輸家。
paras_en: The Democrats won both chambers of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections, and U.S. stocks rose on Wednesday, but some AI‑related stocks fell against the trend. Wall Street analysts say the election outcome could impose more constraints on data‑center construction, though the demand for compute power remains, and the real variables are construction speed, cost, and whether slower investment can ease market concerns about excessive borrowing.

According to Bloomberg, while the Nasdaq‑100 index rose more than 1%, AI‑related shares such as CoreWeave (CRWV‑US), Nvidia (NVDA‑US) and Marvell (MRVL‑US) slipped. Analysts see the election bringing policy risk and prompting the industry to re‑examine spending discipline.

Demand Won’t Disappear; Data Centers May Be Built More Slowly and Expensively

Truist’s chief investment officer and head of market strategy Keith Lerner says the election adds uncertainty to the path and pace of data‑center development, but the massive compute demand will still drive construction. Companies may face changes to tax incentives, local opposition, the need to relocate sites, or tighter restrictions and conditions.

Wealthspire’s chief investment officer Brad Long notes that the Texas election results could make politicians from both parties pay more attention to anti‑data‑center sentiment. To secure re‑election, more local officials may follow suit, advocating to protect communities from data‑center expansion.

He argues the market’s issue to digest isn’t whether data centers will be built, but “where they’ll be built, how long it will take, and how many regulatory hurdles must be cleared.” Those frictions could delay capital spending and push back the timeline for realizing AI investment returns.

RWA Wealth Partners’ chief investment officer JP Powers thinks market worries may be overstated and existing projects are unlikely to be heavily impacted. Still, if developers have to increase local contributions or comply with more regulations, construction and operating costs could rise.

A slower expansion isn’t necessarily all bad; it could ease cash‑burn pressure

Nomura cross‑asset strategist Charlie McElligott offers another view: if the election forces U.S. data‑center builds to slow down, it may temper the race among large cloud providers to pour capital into capacity, reducing market concerns about massive debt issuance, equity financing and free‑cash‑flow consumption.

That is one reason why post‑election markets might remain relatively optimistic. Previously, investors had begun worrying that the scale of AI investment was inflating faster than financing could match the expected returns.

Interactive Brokers’ chief strategist Steve Sosnick says concerns about overly aggressive spending and large borrowing by providers are justified. If construction pace becomes more manageable, it may hurt suppliers but could impose financial discipline that the market is willing to accept.

He also points out that data‑center construction already has strong momentum and involves many jobs, and the election of several governors and the shift in congressional power are unlikely to halt overall development entirely.

Year‑end rally faces headwinds; tech stocks need careful winner selection

Miller Tabak chief market strategist Matt Maley warns that growing obstacles for the AI sector could make it harder for the typical year‑end rally seen in midterm election years. He expects anti‑data‑center sentiment to quickly become a campaign issue in the 2028 election.

RBC Capital Markets U.S. equities strategist Lori Calvasina says that even without clear congressional action, the governor races still create policy risk because AI and data centers have become key issues in heated contests. She remains cautious about whether the election can serve as a turning point that removes market risk.

JPMorgan (JPM‑US) global markets intelligence head Andrew Tyler maintains a short‑term bullish stance on tech stocks. He notes that Texas gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa proposes pausing data‑center construction before new rules are set, but the actual impact is open to interpretation.

One scenario is that existing projects and permits continue while new plans shift to other states; another is an overall slowdown that curtails capital spending. Tyler says he won’t abandon tech‑stock trading, still expects tactical rebounds, but markets may become pickier about winners and losers in the tech and AI space.

items.title: 敗選也傷荷包！川普媒體股價跌破歷史低點 迷因幣重挫逾10%
items.title_en: Election Loss Also Hits Wallets! Trump Media Stock Falls Below Historic Low, Meme Coin Plummets Over 10%
paras: 民主黨在美國期中選舉大勝、拿下國會兩院後，與總統川普相關的資產遭到拋售。川普媒體與科技集團(DJT-US)周三(4日)股價觸及歷史新低，川普迷因幣也重挫，反映投資人擔心，川普家族的商業利益將面臨新一輪國會監督。
據外媒報導，旗下擁有社群平台Truth Social的川普媒體，股價盤中一度跌至5.03美元，創歷史新低。根據CoinMarketCap數據，川普在第二任就職前幾天推出的迷因幣$TRUMP，過去24小時跌幅超過10%。
這兩項資產的交易都高度受到散戶投機活動影響，同步下跌顯示，市場正重新評估選舉結果對川普相關企業的衝擊。過去數月，民主黨已多次表態，若取得任一國會議院控制權，將尋求調查川普及其家族的商業利益，讓與第一家庭有關的企業都可能成為調查對象。
預料將出任眾議院監督委員會主席的加州民主黨眾議員Robert Garcia，周二晚間隨著選舉結果陸續揭曉，在社群媒體發文寫道：「找好律師吧。」
相關事業是川普家族財富的重要來源。根據彭博億萬富豪指數，川普透過由長子小唐納控制的信託，持有價值約6億美元的川普媒體股份；迷因幣事業則占其財富約8,300萬美元。
川普第二任期陸續拓展新事業，成為其任內備受關注的現象。他在任期間從加密貨幣及冠有其名的商業活動獲利，打破美國總統數十年來的慣例，也引發左派對利益衝突的批評。
今年稍早，《紐約時報》詢問川普第二任期的利益衝突問題時，他回答：「我發現根本沒人在乎。」白宮則持續強調，總統的商業活動並不存在利益衝突。
然而，選前民調顯示，政府貪腐是選民高度關切的議題。福斯新聞民調發現，60%選民對政府貪腐極度擔憂；蓋洛普調查則顯示，89%受訪者認為美國政府貪腐普遍，反映民眾對政府貪腐的觀感達到20年來最嚴重的程度。
paras_en: After the Democrats’ sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections and gaining control of both chambers of Congress, assets tied to former President Trump have been sold off. Trump Media & Technology Group (DJT‑US) saw its share price hit a historic low on Wednesday (the 4th), and the Trump meme coin also tumbled, reflecting investors’ worries that the Trump family’s business interests will face a new round of congressional oversight.

According to foreign media reports, Trump Media, which owns the social platform Truth Social, saw its stock dip intraday to $5.03, a record low. CoinMarketCap data shows that the $TRUMP meme coin, launched just days before Trump’s second inauguration, fell more than 10% in the past 24 hours.

Both assets are heavily influenced by retail speculation, and their simultaneous decline indicates the market is re‑evaluating the election’s impact on Trump‑related companies. In recent months the Democrats have repeatedly said that if they gain control of either house of Congress they will seek investigations into Trump and his family’s business interests, putting any enterprise linked to the First Family at risk of scrutiny.

California Democrat Representative Robert Garcia, who is expected to become chair of the House Oversight Committee, posted on social media on Tuesday night as election results continued to roll in, writing: “Find a good lawyer.”

These businesses are a major source of the Trump family’s wealth. Bloomberg’s Billionaires Index estimates that Trump, through a trust controlled by his eldest son Donald Jr., holds about $600 million worth of Trump Media shares; the meme‑coin venture accounts for roughly $83 million of his fortune.

Trump’s second term has seen a steady rollout of new ventures, becoming a hallmark of his presidency. He profited from cryptocurrency and other commercial activities bearing his name, breaking decades‑long norms for U.S. presidents and drawing left‑wing criticism over potential conflicts of interest.

Earlier this year, when The New York Times asked about conflicts of interest in his second term, Trump replied, “I find that nobody really cares.” The White House continues to stress that the president’s business activities do not constitute a conflict of interest.

However, pre‑election polls show that government corruption is a top concern for voters. A Fox News poll found that 60% of respondents are extremely worried about government corruption; a Gallup survey showed 89% believe corruption is widespread in the U.S. government, marking the highest level of public concern in two decades.

items.title: 〈美國期中選舉〉政治押注失靈？加密業關鍵選戰敗北 比特幣卻重返8萬美元
items.title_en: U.S. Midterm Election: Political Bets Falter? Crypto Industry Loses Key Races While Bitcoin Reclaims $80,000
paras: 加密貨幣產業在本屆美國期中選舉投入約2億美元，雖然支持的候選人大多勝出，卻在幾場重金布局的關鍵選戰失利。隨著民主黨拿下國會兩院，業界不僅面臨推動立法的阻力，也可能因與總統川普的密切關係，遭遇更嚴格的國會監督與調查。
最受矚目的挫敗出現在俄亥俄州。對加密貨幣抱持懷疑態度的民主黨人布朗(Sherrod Brown)以明顯優勢勝選，重返參議院，儘管加密貨幣政治行動委員會投入逾6,000萬美元試圖阻止他當選，仍未能奏效。

重金阻擋布朗失敗 關鍵選戰考驗政治影響力

俄亥俄州這場選戰是美國參議院史上最昂貴的選戰之一，也被視為檢驗加密貨幣產業政治影響力的重要指標。今年9月，參議院因民主黨反對，未能推進加密貨幣重要法案《Clarity Act》，已讓與川普關係日益密切的業界遭受打擊。
部分進步派民主黨候選人也在初選期間，成功以對手與加密貨幣產業的關係作為攻擊主軸。道明考恩分析師Jaret Seiberg在周二報告中表示，這些發展正使加密貨幣面對的政治環境惡化，也讓部分遊說人士質疑業界是否押對候選人。
不過，業界並非全面失利。主要超級政治行動委員會Fairshake及其關聯組織，投入至少1,350萬美元阻擋內布拉斯加州獨立參議員候選人Dan Osborn，最終由曾支持《Clarity Act》的共和黨現任參議員Pete Ricketts勝出。
Fairshake主要金主包括Coinbase(COIN-US)、瑞波公司及創投公司Andreessen Horowitz。該組織支持32名眾議員候選人，包括19名共和黨人及13名民主黨人，篩選依據是對方是否支持產業的優先政策。
截至報導時，Fairshake投入資金的34場選戰中，已拿下29場，部分選戰仍未揭曉；但在投入至少100萬美元支持的6名眾議員候選人中，目前僅3人勝出，顯示整體勝率未能完全反映重點布局的成效。

民主黨掌國會添監管變數 比特幣收復跌勢

加密貨幣產業在過去兩個選舉周期合計投入約5億美元，試圖建立跨黨派國會盟友。2024年，業界協助數十名友善候選人當選，這些議員後來共同推動通過促進美元穩定幣採用的法律。
然而，《Clarity Act》推進受阻，加上民主黨取得國會控制權，意味產業接下來可能面臨更嚴格的監督，尤其是業界與川普之間的關係，以及川普涉及的加密貨幣商業活動。
Fairshake發言人Geoff Vetter表示，新當選與現任議員將面臨選擇，是保護消費者與美國就業，還是阻擋進步，顯示業界仍將持續爭取政策支持。
加密貨幣在選舉結果出爐後一度於隔夜下跌，但周三收復失地。比特幣截至報導時上漲3.1%，回到8萬美元以上，市場反應並未一路延續最初的悲觀情緒。
瑞波公司法務長Stu Alderoty在開票前表示，相較兩年前，加密貨幣產業的處境已有天壤之別。不過，談到民主黨可能調查川普的加密貨幣交易時，他也坦言，相關跡象已相當明顯。
paras_en: The crypto industry spent about $200 million on this U.S. midterm cycle; although most of the candidates it backed won, it lost several high‑stakes, heavily funded contests. With Democrats taking control of both chambers, the sector now faces not only legislative resistance but also the prospect of stricter congressional oversight and investigations due to its close ties with former President Trump.

The most notable setback occurred in Ohio. Democrat Sherrod Brown, who is skeptical of crypto, won a decisive victory to return to the Senate, despite the Crypto Political Action Committee pouring more than $60 million into efforts to block his election, which proved ineffective.

Heavy spending to stop Brown failed – the Ohio race was one of the most expensive Senate contests in history and is seen as a litmus test of crypto’s political clout. In September, Democrats blocked the Senate from advancing the pivotal “Clarity Act,” dealing a blow to an industry increasingly aligned with Trump.

Some progressive Democratic candidates also used their opponents’ ties to the crypto industry as a primary attack line during the primaries. Dominion analyst Jaret Seiberg said in a Tuesday report that these developments are worsening the political environment for crypto and prompting lobbyists to question whether the industry backed the right candidates.

Nevertheless, the industry did not lose across the board. The major super‑PAC Fairshake and its affiliates spent at least $13.5 million to oppose independent Senate candidate Dan Osborn in Nebraska, a race ultimately won by Republican incumbent Pete Ricketts, who had previously supported the “Clarity Act.”

Fairshake’s principal backers include Coinbase (COIN‑US), Ripple and venture firm Andreessen Horowitz. The group backs 32 House candidates – 19 Republicans and 13 Democrats – selected based on their support for the industry’s priority policies.

At the time of reporting, Fairshake had invested in 34 races, winning 29 of them, with some outcomes still pending; however, of the six House candidates it backed with at least $1 million each, only three have won so far, indicating that overall win rates do not fully reflect the impact of its targeted spending.

Democratic control of Congress adds regulatory uncertainty while Bitcoin rebounds. Over the past two election cycles the crypto sector has poured roughly $500 million into building bipartisan allies. In 2024 the industry helped dozens of friendly candidates get elected, who later worked together to pass legislation promoting the adoption of dollar‑stablecoins.

But the stalled “Clarity Act” and Democratic dominance in Congress suggest the industry may face tighter scrutiny, especially regarding its relationship with Trump and the former president’s crypto‑related business activities.

Fairshake spokesperson Geoff Vetter said newly elected and incumbent lawmakers will have to choose between protecting consumers and U.S. jobs or blocking progress, underscoring that the industry will continue to fight for policy support.

Crypto prices dipped overnight after the election results were announced but recovered on Wednesday. Bitcoin was up 3.1% at the time of reporting, climbing back above $80,000, and the market did not sustain the initial pessimism.

Ripple’s chief legal officer Stu Alderoty said that, compared with two years ago, the crypto industry’s situation has changed dramatically. He added that signs are already clear that Democrats may investigate Trump’s crypto transactions.

items.title: AI股選後能翻身？小摩看科技股反彈 加碼先看四大訊號
items.title_en: Can AI Stocks Recover After the Election? JPMorgan Sees Tech Bounce, Looks for Four Key Signals Before Adding More
paras: 美國期中選舉結果出爐後，美股周三(4日)扭轉稍早跌勢走高。摩根大通(JPM-US)交易部門認為，近期遭到拋售的科技股有望迎來短線反彈，市場漲勢也可能從少數大型權值股，擴散至更多產業。不過，團隊尚未全面看多AI交易，配置上仍較偏重景氣循環股。
由Andrew Tyler領軍的美國市場情報團隊在周三報告中表示：「我們不會放棄科技股交易，並會布局戰術性反彈。」團隊建議採取槓鈴式策略，同時配置科技股與景氣循環股，但給予後者較高權重。

科技股有望反彈 AI加碼仍待四大訊號

民主黨取得國會控制權後，投資人持續評估科技業面臨的政策變化，尤其是AI基礎建設支出前景。德州州長當選人Gina Hinojosa主張，在建立更多規範前立即暫停新資料中心建設，一度引發隔夜賣壓。不過，以科技股為主的那斯達克100指數周三轉而上漲1.8%。
摩根大通交易部門認為，市場對德州政策可能轉向的疑慮或許過大，因為資料中心仍可選擇在其他州興建，新規也不代表所有建設都將完全停擺。
儘管看好短線反彈，團隊並未對AI交易全面亮綠燈。投資人在重新增加曝險前，仍希望看到幾項訊號，包括市場持倉充分出清、大型雲端業者確認資本支出計畫、半導體與記憶體企業交出正面財報，以及資本市場活動改善。
這也意味著，科技股回升不等於AI相關企業將全面受惠。隨著市場更加重視投資回報與資金來源，投資人將更仔細區分AI產業的贏家與輸家。
巴克萊同日上午也提醒，選舉結果本身不足以替美股掃除年底上漲的障礙，顯示華爾街對選後行情能否持續仍有不同看法。
科技業之外，摩根大通交易部門也關注，民主黨是否會推動結束與伊朗的衝突。團隊指出，新一屆國會明年1月就任後，議員可能採取撤回資金支持或要求撤軍等措施，針對未獲國會授權、持續逾90天的軍事衝突施壓。該行認為，市場似乎正逐漸反映達成協議的可能性。

選後漲勢可望擴散 偏好消費與金融股

歷史表現則為團隊的樂觀看法提供另一項依據。報告引述摩根大通Craig Cohen的統計指出，自1950年以來，每次期中選舉隔年，標普500指數均上漲，平均漲幅約15%。
若觀察選舉後不同期間，標普500過去在三個月內平均上漲5.4%，六個月內上漲11.4%，九個月內上漲12.5%。這些歷史數據為選後行情提供參考，但並非未來報酬的保證。
整體而言，團隊預期漲勢將擴及更多產業，但能源股的上漲空間相對有限，科技股下跌空間則可能縮小。在景氣循環類股中，團隊偏好消費與金融股，尤其是在殖利率曲線持續變陡的情境下。
paras_en: After the U.S. midterm election results were announced, U.S. equities reversed earlier losses and rose on Wednesday, the 4th. JPMorgan (JPM-US) trading desk believes that tech stocks recently sold off could see a short‑term rebound, and the market rally may spread from a few large‑cap names to more sectors. However, the team is not fully bullish on AI trades yet and still leans toward cyclical stocks in its allocation.

The U.S. market intelligence team led by Andrew Tyler said in its Wednesday report: “We are not abandoning tech trading and will position for a tactical rebound.” The team recommends a barbell approach, allocating to both tech and cyclical stocks but giving the latter a higher weight.

Tech stocks could bounce, but AI upgrades still await four key signals. After Democrats took control of Congress, investors continue to assess policy changes facing the tech sector, especially the outlook for AI infrastructure spending. Texas governor‑elect Gina Hinojosa has advocated pausing new data‑center construction until more regulations are in place, which sparked overnight selling pressure. Nonetheless, the Nasdaq‑100, which is tech‑heavy, rose 1.8% on Wednesday.

JPMorgan’s trading desk thinks market concerns about a possible shift in Texas policy may be overstated, since data centers can be built in other states and new rules do not mean all projects will be halted.

While optimistic about a short‑term bounce, the team has not given a full green light to AI trades. Before investors increase exposure again, they want to see several signals: market positions fully cleared, major cloud providers confirming cap‑ex plans, semiconductor and memory companies delivering positive earnings, and an improvement in capital‑market activity.

This also means a tech‑stock rally does not automatically translate into a broad benefit for AI‑related firms. As the market focuses more on returns and funding sources, investors will scrutinize winners and losers within the AI industry more closely.

Barclays also warned that the election outcome alone is insufficient to clear the path for year‑end equity gains, indicating that Wall Street remains divided on whether post‑election momentum can be sustained.

Beyond tech, JPMorgan’s trading desk is watching whether Democrats will push to end the conflict with Iran. The team notes that after the new Congress takes office in January, lawmakers may move to withdraw funding or demand troop withdrawals, pressuring a war that has lasted over 90 days without congressional authorization. The bank believes the market is gradually pricing in the possibility of a deal.

Historical performance provides another basis for the team’s optimism. The report cites JPMorgan’s Craig Cohen, who notes that since 1950, the S&P 500 has risen in the year following every midterm election, with an average gain of about 15%.

Looking at different post‑election horizons, the S&P 500 has historically risen an average of 5.4% in the first three months, 11.4% in six months and 12.5% in nine months. These figures offer context for post‑election market behavior but are not guarantees of future returns.

Overall, the team expects the rally to spread to more sectors, though energy stocks have limited upside and the downside potential for tech may shrink. Within cyclical stocks, the team favors consumer and financial stocks, especially as the yield curve continues to steepen.

items.title: 「敗選就是因為戰爭！」范斯開砲 美油重挫跌破90美元
items.title_en: "Our Defeat Is Because of the War!" Vance Fires Shots, US Oil Plummets Below $90
paras: 美國副總統范斯(JD Vance)周三(4日)將共和黨期中選舉慘敗歸咎於對伊朗戰爭，加上川普表態暫無立即攻擊伊朗的計畫，市場押注選舉挫敗將促使白宮尋求外交解決方案，帶動國際油價重挫，西德州原油跌破每桶90美元。
美國西德州中級原油(WTI)下跌7%，報每桶89.40美元；國際基準布蘭特原油期貨下跌近8%，報每桶95.41美元。隨著美伊高層近期均釋出願意透過外交解決衝突的訊號，原油期貨本周以來跌幅已超過14%。
范斯周三在社群平台發文表示：「我們敗選的原因就是這場戰爭，總統本人昨晚也這麼說。」他指出，許多2024年支持川普的選民，似乎因不滿戰爭而在這次選舉中轉離共和黨。
民主黨在周二選舉拿下參眾兩院，取得向川普施壓、要求結束戰爭的政治籌碼。這場衝突已擾亂全球能源供應長達八個月，推升汽油與柴油價格，也加深美國選民對生活成本的不滿。
交易員目前似乎押注，共和黨敗選將迫使川普與伊朗談判。川普周二接受《金融時報》訪問時表示，目前沒有立即對伊朗發動攻擊的計畫，緩解市場對選後戰事升級的擔憂。
此前，油市因預期選舉結束後可能爆發更大規模衝突，已將部分升級風險反映在價格中，帶動油價10月上漲逾10%。如今，選舉結果與白宮官員的公開表態，促使交易員迅速調整部位。
加拿大帝國商業銀行(CM-US)資深能源交易員Rebecca Babin表示，出乎預期的選舉結果使市場情緒高漲，油市正處於「先開槍、再問問題」的交易模式。
她指出，原先不少觀察人士認為，民主黨壓倒性勝選可能促使川普升高對伊朗的軍事行動，但范斯的言論，以及關鍵盟友未公開表態支持升級戰事，都對這項假設構成挑戰。
范斯也表示，支持戰爭的人可以主張，付出選舉失利的代價仍然值得，但應坦承這項取捨。他強調，所有人都知道共和黨為何落敗，而任何關於未來方向的誠實討論，都必須從這個原因開始。
paras_en: U.S. Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday (the 4th) blamed the Republican Party’s midterm election loss on the war with Iran, and with President Trump saying there are no immediate plans to attack Iran, the market is betting that the electoral setback will push the White House toward a diplomatic solution, sending international oil prices tumbling and West Texas crude falling below $90 a barrel.

West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell 7% to $89.40 a barrel, while the benchmark Brent crude futures dropped nearly 8% to $95.41 a barrel. As senior U.S. and Iranian officials have recently signaled a willingness to resolve the conflict diplomatically, oil futures have fallen more than 14% this week.

Vance posted on social media on Wednesday, "The reason we lost the election is this war; the President himself said so last night." He noted that many 2024 Trump supporters appear to have left the GOP in this election because they were dissatisfied with the war.

Democrats on Tuesday captured both houses of Congress, gaining political leverage to pressure Trump to end the war. The conflict has disrupted global energy supplies for eight months, driving up gasoline and diesel prices and deepening U.S. voters’ frustration over living costs.

Traders now seem to be betting that the GOP’s loss will force Trump to negotiate with Iran. In a Financial Times interview on Tuesday, Trump said there are currently no plans for an immediate attack on Iran, easing market fears of post‑election escalation.

Earlier, the oil market had priced in the risk of a larger conflict after the election, which had helped push oil prices up more than 10% in October. The election outcome and public statements from White House officials have now prompted traders to quickly adjust their positions.
Rebecca Babin, a senior energy trader at CIBC (CM‑US), said the unexpected election result has lifted market sentiment, and the oil market is now in a "shoot first, ask questions later" trading mode.

She added that many observers had initially thought a Democratic landslide could push Trump to intensify military action against Iran, but Vance’s comments and the lack of public support for escalation from key allies challenge that assumption.

Vance also said that supporters of the war can argue that paying the price of an electoral loss is still worthwhile, but they must acknowledge that trade‑off. He stressed that everyone knows why the GOP lost, and any honest discussion about the future must start with that reason.

paras_en: According to CNBC on the 4th, the Democratic Party captured both chambers of the US Congress in the midterm elections. With former President Trump saying he accepts the results, political uncertainty on Wall Street eased, and US stock futures rebounded sharply after a steep overnight drop, with Dow futures jumping more than 800 points. However, the market remains wary of tighter data‑center regulation, putting pressure on AI‑infrastructure stocks.

Yongfeng Bank held a press conference on the evening of the 4th regarding the abnormal transfer incident that occurred on the 3rd. The investigation found that an external hacker exploited a security‑setting vulnerability in the supplier of its new online‑banking transaction system. Chairman Cao Weishi and General Manager Zhuang Mingfu personally apologized to affected customers and the public, stating that although no financial loss occurred, the damage to the bank’s reputation was substantial. Yongfeng has now taken the system offline and is gathering evidence to pursue legal compensation against the foreign software supplier.

Advantech (2395‑TW) held a legal‑presentation meeting on the 4th. The company is optimistic that fourth‑quarter revenue will remain at a high level and may surpass the third‑quarter peak, and based on current order visibility, the outlook for next year is positive, with revenue expected to grow at a high double‑digit rate. In addition, economies of scale are beginning to show, so profit growth is expected to outpace revenue growth as a new normal.

Integrated circuit test‑maker Siliconware Precision Industries (6257‑TW) announced October revenue of NT$2.1 billion on the 4th, marking month‑over‑month and year‑over‑year growth and setting a new monthly record for the fourth consecutive month with revenue exceeding NT$2 billion. Siliconware said that with its deployment of photonic integrated circuit (PIC) and optical‑engine testing technologies, AI‑related product share is expected to break the 30% threshold.

During intraday trading on the 4th, the Taiwan stock index fell sharply, breaking the 42,000‑point level as the US midterm results and weakening US futures weighed on sentiment. The index swung a total of 1,885 points, the fourth‑largest intraday swing on record, and closed at 42,948 points with turnover reaching NT$1.1 trillion. Foreign investors withdrew about NT$149.8 billion, marking the fifth‑largest single‑day net sell‑off in history, heavily selling the actively managed ETF Active Unified Upgrade 50 (00403A‑TW) with 84,000 lots, followed by the Yuanta Taiwan 50 (0050‑TW) with 77,000 lots, and in individual stocks, the 19‑strike put options on TSMC (2330‑TW) were the most sold.

paras: 美國期中選舉結果逐步明朗，民主黨選情優於預期，惟川普立即表態願與民主黨合作，消弭選舉爭議的極端情境發生，市場焦點也從選舉結果轉向政策與產業影響。凱基銀行財富管理處表示，在重大立法仍受行政權制衡下，未來華府政策角力可能升溫，留意川普是否更傾向轉移焦點，加大國際事務的參與。此外，AI監管、反壟斷及資料中心等議題，也將成為科技產業新變數。
股市方面，選舉效應雖可能放大科技股短期波動，但不致改變AI長期發展趨勢，畢竟AI是國力的象徵，無論民主或共和兩黨都不會坐視其他強權超車的可能。配置可聚焦獲利穩健、監管曝險較低的科技龍頭，並搭配醫療保健、消費及電力相關公用事業等防禦型類股，提升投資組合的韌性。
債市則受惠財政擴張預期降溫，10年期美債殖利率已回落至4.9%附近；在殖利率仍處相對高檔下，可分批布局中長天期投資等級債，掌握收益的機會。美元短線則偏弱整理，預估美元指數於100至103區間震盪。
整體而言，選後投資主軸正從「押注選舉」轉向掌握基本面與資產配置，透過股債均衡與產業分散，更有機會在波動中掌握下一階段契機。
paras_en: The results of the US midterm elections are becoming clearer, with the Democratic Party performing better than expected. However, former President Trump immediately stated his willingness to cooperate with the Democrats to avoid an extreme scenario of election‑related disputes. Market focus has therefore shifted from the election outcome to policy and industry impacts. KGI Bank’s wealth management division notes that, while major legislation will still be checked by the executive branch, policy battles in Washington could intensify. Investors should watch whether Trump leans more toward shifting the focus to greater involvement in international affairs. In addition, AI regulation, antitrust issues and data‑center developments will become new variables for the technology sector.

Although the election effect may amplify short‑term volatility in tech stocks, it will not alter the long‑term development trend of AI, which remains a symbol of national power. Both Democrats and Republicans are unlikely to sit idle while rival powers try to overtake them. Portfolio allocation can concentrate on profitable, well‑regulated tech leaders, complemented by defensive sectors such as healthcare, consumer staples and utilities related to electricity, to enhance portfolio resilience.

The bond market is benefiting from a cooling of fiscal‑expansion expectations, with the 10‑year US Treasury yield having fallen back to around 4.9%. With yields still relatively high, investors can stagger purchases of intermediate‑ to long‑term investment‑grade bonds to capture yield opportunities. The US dollar is showing short‑term weakness and is expected to trade in a range of 100 to 103 on the dollar index.

Overall, post‑election investment focus is shifting from “betting on the election” to capturing fundamentals and asset allocation. By balancing equities and bonds and diversifying across industries, investors have a better chance of seizing the next wave of opportunities amid market volatility.

items.title_en: U.S. Midterm Election: Chinese Netizens Mock Trump's Crushing Defeat! Beijing Still Hopes for Cooperation, $14 B Taiwan Arms Sale Draws Attention
paras: 美國共和黨期中選舉慘敗後，「川普大敗」相關話題在中國微博迅速發酵，截至周三(4日)晚間累積逾7,000萬次瀏覽。不過，北京官方隨即釋出維持合作的訊號，顯示即使川普政治實力受挫，中國仍期待透過兩國領袖互動，延續美中關係的穩定局面。
這場選舉也為兩周後登場、今年第三次川習會增添變數。川普在國會的影響力減弱，可能使對中強硬派帶來更多壓力，牽動晶片出口管制與對台政策，也讓北京重新評估他能兌現多少談判承諾。

網友熱議川普慘敗 北京強調合作照常

中國外交部發言人毛寧在例行記者會上，將期中選舉形容為美國「內政」，並強調中方願推進川普與習近平達成的共識，擴大合作，建立相互尊重、和平共處、合作共贏的美中關係。
這與中國社群平台上的反應形成對比。一名擁有400萬名追蹤者的微博評論者批評，川普敗選顯示，煽動情緒與製造分裂並非可持續的治理方式，「讓美國再次偉大」已淪為空洞口號。
川普重返白宮後，美中曾在2025年爆發全面貿易戰，關稅稅率一度升至三位數。但雙方隨後穩住關係，《彭博》指出，華府在晶片限制與對台支持方面也展現克制。
清華大學國際安全與戰略研究中心主任達巍認為，整體穩定至少可維持至川普本屆任期結束，但在這個架構下，來自美國國會的雜音與壓力將增加。

川普成對中強硬派制衡 晶片與軍售仍有分歧

兩年前以加強對中經濟對抗姿態勝選的川普，如今反而成為牽制部分對中立場更強硬議員的力量。國會目前有多項待審法案，旨在收緊美國出口管制。
例如《MATCH法案》將要求政府辨識應受限制的晶片設備與中國製造設施，並推動盟友採取與美國企業面臨規範同樣嚴格的管制措施。
台灣也是美中關係的核心分歧。報導指出，川普政府在去年12月批准創紀錄的對台軍售後，目前仍暫緩一項規模140億美元的對台軍售案。北京持續要求華府停止對台軍售，美國《台灣關係法》則要求提供台灣維持足夠自衛能力所需的防禦性武器。
中國全球化智庫創辦人王輝耀認為，歷經近十年的貿易衝突，美中已形成任何一方施壓都可能造成雙方受損的局面，這種新平衡將迫使兩國務實合作。

國會影響力下降 川習談判承諾更難兌現

川普與習近平9月會面時延長貿易休戰，為雙方爭取更多時間，但台灣與AI發展等議題仍存在明顯分歧。
中國官媒《環球時報》前總編輯胡錫進也預期，川普將尋求維持對中關係穩定。他認為，目前的平衡來自雙方實力較量，美國內部政治鬥爭加劇，不會讓華府獲得更多對中施壓工具。
不過，川普進入任期後半段，外交仍是他能掌握的重要政策工具，若試圖藉此另闢施政戰場，仍可能帶來新的動盪。
北京胡同研究創辦合夥人馮楚誠指出，川普仍有相當大的空間與習近平談判，但向北京兌現部分承諾的能力將受到更多限制。這雖縮小雙方討價還價的空間，也讓潛在美中協議的界線更加清楚。
paras_en: After the Republican Party’s crushing loss in the U.S. midterm elections, the "Trump disaster" trend quickly went viral on Chinese Weibo, accumulating more than 70 million views by Wednesday night (the 4th). Yet Beijing immediately signaled a desire to maintain cooperation, indicating that despite Trump’s political setback, China still expects to keep U.S.-China relations stable through leader‑to‑leader interaction.

The election also adds uncertainty to the third Trump‑Xi summit scheduled two weeks later. With Trump’s influence in Congress waning, hard‑liners on China may face more pressure, affecting chip export controls and Taiwan policy, and prompting Beijing to reassess how many of his negotiation promises can be fulfilled.

Netizens heatedly discuss Trump’s defeat while Beijing stresses that cooperation continues as usual. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning described the midterms as a U.S. domestic affair and emphasized China’s willingness to advance the consensus reached between Trump and Xi, expanding cooperation and building a U.S.-China relationship based on mutual respect, peaceful coexistence and win‑win outcomes.

This contrasts with reactions on Chinese social platforms. A Weibo commentator with 4 million followers criticized that Trump’s loss shows that inflaming emotions and sowing division is not a sustainable governing method, and that “Make America Great Again” has become an empty slogan.

After Trump returned to the White House, the U.S. and China briefly entered a full‑blown trade war in 2025, with tariff rates soaring into triple digits. Relations later steadied; Bloomberg noted that Washington showed restraint on chip restrictions and support for Taiwan.

Da Wei, director of Tsinghua University’s Center for International Security and Strategy, believes overall stability can last at least until the end of Trump’s current term, but within that framework, noise and pressure from the U.S. Congress will increase.

Trump now serves as a counterweight to hard‑line China hawks in Congress, even though he won two years ago on a platform of tougher economic confrontation with China. Several bills pending in Congress aim to tighten U.S. export controls.

For example, the MATCH Act would require the government to identify chip equipment and Chinese‑manufactured facilities subject to restrictions and push allies to adopt equally stringent controls on U.S. firms.

Taiwan remains a core flashpoint in U.S.-China relations. Reports say that after the Trump administration approved a record‑size arms sale to Taiwan in December last year, it has now put on hold a $14 billion arms package for the island. Beijing continues to demand Washington stop arms sales to Taiwan, while the U.S. Taiwan Relations Act obliges the U.S. to provide defensive weapons necessary for Taiwan’s self‑defense.

Wang Huiyao, founder of the Globalization Institute, argues that after nearly a decade of trade conflict, the U.S. and China have reached a new balance where pressure from either side would hurt both, forcing pragmatic cooperation.

Congress’s diminished influence makes it harder for Trump and Xi to honor their negotiation commitments. When Trump and Xi met in September, they extended the trade truce to buy more time, but disagreements over Taiwan and AI development remain evident.

Hu Xijin, former editor‑in‑chief of the Global Times, also expects Trump to seek stability in relations with China. He believes the current balance stems from a power contest, and intensified U.S. domestic political fighting will not give Washington additional leverage over China.
Nevertheless, as Trump moves into the second half of his term, diplomacy remains a key tool at his disposal; using it to open a new policy front could still generate fresh turbulence.

Feng Chucheng, co‑founder of Beijing Hutong Research, notes that Trump still has considerable room to negotiate with Xi, but his ability to deliver on promises to Beijing will face tighter constraints, narrowing the bargaining space and clarifying the limits of any prospective U.S.-China agreement.

items.title: 〈群電法說〉筆電產業提前進入淡季 Q4通訊、AI伺服器電源成營運支柱
items.title_en: <PowerTech Earnings Call> Laptop Industry Enters Off‑Season Early; Q4 Telecom and AI Server Power Supplies Become Operational Pillars
paras: 電源廠群電(6412-TW)今(4)日召開法說，筆電產業記憶體缺貨問題短期內仍難以改善、提前進入淡季，不過，非筆電電源業務可望成為支撐營運的重要動能，看好第四季通訊電源及AI伺服器電源表現，隨新產品陸續放量，通訊電源營收力拚較上季及去年同期倍數成長。
群電亦公布10月自結合併營收，受PC品牌客戶提前啟動庫存調整影響，拉貨動能較上月衰退，單月合併營收19.23億元；累計今年1至10月合併營收255.64億元，年減12.1%。
群電表示，筆電產業記憶體缺貨問題短期內仍難以改善，市場甚至出現旺季不旺、提前轉淡的現象。過去第三季底至第四季初通常為品牌客戶備貨旺季，但今年受到半導體供應吃緊及供應鏈資源調度影響，品牌客戶自10月起提前進入淡季，並陸續進行庫存調整，短期接單及拉貨力道相對保守。
在非筆電電源業務方面，伺服器電源雖受到關鍵零組件缺料及測試設備短缺影響，部分客戶拉貨時程遞延，但市場需求仍維持強勁，隨著新專案持續導入，業務動能穩步提升。
通訊電源則展現強勁成長動能，全系列產品需求熱絡，客戶持續追加訂單，整體訂單需求遠超原先產能規劃。除了應用於商用、車載及機載的高效能移動天線電源需求持續擴大外，新世代家用接收器電源也已於9月順利量產，第四季出貨量可望進一步提升。
因應客戶強勁拉貨需求，群電表示，已積極加速備料並提升產能，全力滿足訂單需求，力拚第四季通訊電源營收較上季及去年同期均呈倍數成長，帶動整體產品組合進一步優化。
paras_en: PowerTech (6412‑TW) held its earnings briefing today (the 4th), noting that the laptop industry’s memory shortage will remain difficult to resolve in the short term and the sector is entering its off‑season early. However, non‑laptop power‑supply business is expected to become a key driver of operations. The company is optimistic about Q4 telecom power supplies and AI server power supplies, and as new products ramp up, telecom power‑supply revenue aims to grow multiple times versus the previous quarter and the same period last year.

PowerTech also released its October consolidated revenue. Due to PC‑brand customers starting inventory adjustments early, the pull‑forward momentum weakened compared with the prior month, resulting in a single‑month consolidated revenue of NT$1.923 billion. Cumulatively, from January to October this year, consolidated revenue was NT$25.564 billion, down 12.1% year‑on‑year.

PowerTech said the laptop‑industry memory shortage will remain hard to alleviate in the short term, and the market even shows a “peak season that isn’t peak” and an early off‑season. Normally, the late Q3 to early Q4 period is a stocking‑up season for brand customers, but this year, tight semiconductor supply and supply‑chain resource allocation forced brand customers to enter the off‑season early from October and gradually adjust inventories, making short‑term order intake and pull‑forward activity relatively cautious.

Regarding non‑laptop power‑supply business, server power supplies have been affected by shortages of key components and testing equipment, causing some customers to delay pull‑forward schedules. Nevertheless, market demand remains strong, and as new projects continue to be introduced, business momentum is steadily improving.

Telecom power supplies are showing strong growth momentum, with robust demand across the entire product range and customers continuously adding orders. Overall order demand far exceeds the original capacity plan. In addition to growing demand for high‑efficiency mobile antenna power supplies used in commercial, automotive and airborne applications, a new generation of home‑receiver power supplies entered mass production successfully in September, and Q4 shipment volumes are expected to rise further.

In response to strong customer pull‑forward demand, PowerTech said it has been actively accelerating material preparation and expanding capacity to fully meet order needs, striving for telecom power‑supply revenue in Q4 to grow multiple times versus both the previous quarter and the same period last year, thereby further optimizing the overall product portfolio.

items.title: 日本升息引爆「全球平倉潮」！人民幣成下一個被借爆的目標？資金外流重創中國外匯！吳嘉隆：股市崩盤？你想太多了！
items.title_en: Japan's Rate Hike Sparks Global Unwinding Wave! Is the Renminbi the Next Target for Massive Borrowing? Capital Outflows Cripple China's FX Reserves! Wu Jialong: Stock Market Crash? You're Overthinking It!
paras: 全球金融市場的敏感神經，再次被東亞兩大貨幣的異常異動狠狠挑動。
一邊是長年維持超寬鬆貨幣政策的日本央行（BOJ），繼 9 月份啟動升息後，市場普遍預期 12 月將再度出手，甚至將基準利率一路推升向 2% 大關；另一邊，則是全球避險基金與跨國套利者，正悄悄將借款目標轉向下一個超低利率貨幣——中國人民幣（RMB）。
「日圓升息會不會再次引爆全球套利交易平倉（Carry Trade Unwind）？股市會不會因此大崩盤？」面對投資人鋪天蓋地的焦慮，總經大師吳嘉隆在《股民想知道》節目中斬釘截鐵地打破市場迷思：「套利交易平倉是必然的，但股市絕對不會崩盤，大家千萬不要把這兩件事硬扯在一起！真正該頭痛的不是全球股市，而是外匯存底即將面臨嚴峻考驗的中國人民銀行！」

一、打破零利率神話！日本央行為何「必須」升息到 2% 以上？
過去數十年，全球投資界最經典的「無風險提款機」，就是利用日本幾乎零成本的資金，向日本銀行大舉借出日圓，再匯往海外購買高殖利率的美債、美股或科技巨頭股票。然而，這個龐大的套利遊戲，正在被日本央行親手終結。
吳嘉隆指出，日本央行這次的升息是「勢在必行、不得不為」：
輸入性通膨失控： 日本過去引以為傲的通縮早已煙消雲散，目前的通膨率長年維持在 2.5%～3% 以上，甚至一度逼近 4%。若基準利率持續停留在 1% 以下的極低水準，實質負利率將持續重創日本國內購買力。
單純干預匯率無效： 美日之間的巨大利差，導致日圓長線面臨毀滅性貶值。日本政府過去試圖靠賣美債、調度美元現金來進場護盤，事實證明根本是杯水車薪。「唯一的解方，就是日本升息幅度必須追上甚至超過美國，徹底把美日利差縮小！」
「利率一定要朝 2% 以上走，雖然對習慣零利率的日本來說很誇張，但只有讓日圓升值，進口物價才會變便宜，才能徹底緩解日本的輸入性通膨，形成實質的經濟良性循環。」吳嘉隆分析。

二、全球平倉潮湧現！吳嘉隆：股市崩盤？你想太多了！
當日本央行堅定走在升息軌道上，國際套利大軍別無選擇，只能展開債務大清理：
投資人必須拋售手上的美元高收益資產；
將資金結匯換回日圓；
匯回日本，清償當初借貸的日圓債務。
這個過程確實會帶來「資金回流日本、推升日圓升值」的效果，但市場隨之而來的恐慌是：「資金撤離美元資產，全球股市會不會崩盤？」
「絕對不會！」 吳嘉隆一針見血地駁斥這種過度恐慌的論調：
「套利平倉只是部分高槓桿投機資金的去槓桿過程。股市的長期走勢，終究取決於企業的基本面與技術革命帶來的實質獲利。把資金結構的調整等同於股市崩盤，完全是你想太多了！」
吳嘉隆強調，當前的股市拉回，本質上是為了消化估值與換手洗籌碼，全球 AI 產業革命的巨額訂單與長線剛需並未消失，絕不可能單純因為日圓套利平倉就走向系統性崩潰。

三、下一個被借爆的目標：人民幣淪為「新提款機」
然而，逐利的資本永遠不會沉睡。當日圓借貸成本攀升、不再便宜時，龐大的跨國套利資金立刻將雷達轉向了全球下一個超低利率的貨幣窪地——人民幣。
吳嘉隆列出一組令人震驚的全球 10 年期公債殖利率對比：
中國 10 年期公債殖利率：約 1.68%
日本 10 年期公債殖利率：約 3.0%
美國 10 年期公債殖利率：約 5.2%
「大家看這個利差有多誘人！」吳嘉隆揭開國際大型銀行與金融機構的套利算盤：中國由於房地產泡沫與實體經濟疲軟，大型國有銀行內部充斥著無處可去的閒置資金。對套利者而言，在中國境內借人民幣的資金成本不到 2%，轉手換成美元匯到海外購買美債，立刻享有超過 5% 的穩健回報！
這種高達 3 個百分點以上的無風險利差，讓人民幣迅速取代日圓，成為新一輪全球套利交易的核心主角。

四、中國人行的噩夢：外匯存底吃不消與「政策兩難」
套利交易的貨幣轉移，對全球股市或許只是資金流向的微調，但對中國人民銀行（央行）而言，卻是一場致命的金融風暴。
吳嘉隆深入剖析，借人民幣套利的標準流程是：在中國境內借出人民幣 ➔ 向中國人行結匯換成美金 ➔ 將美金匯往海外投資。
這將對中國帶來兩大毀滅性的連鎖衝擊：
外匯儲備面臨劇烈消耗：大量的資金藉由套利管道合法外逃，等於天天在搬走中國人行寶貴的美元外匯存底。一旦外匯儲備降至安全警戒線之下，將嚴重削弱中國防禦匯率風險與進口民生物資的能力。
陷入無法自拔的貨幣政策兩難：
若為了救實體經濟而降息： 境內利差進一步擴大，只會加速資金外逃、引發人民幣斷崖式貶值；
若為了阻止資金外流而升息： 本已瀕臨窒息的中國房地產與內需製造業，將在資金成本上升的重壓下徹底崩潰！
「實體經濟差，照理說應該降息貶值刺激出口；但資金瘋狂外逃擠壓外匯存底，又逼得你必須升息護匯。中國的貨幣政策接下來將陷入極其痛苦的矛盾，最終恐怕只能祭出更殘酷的『鐵腕資本管制』來硬封鎖！」

結語：看懂資金大遷徙，抓準長多免驚慌
金融市場的每一次政策轉向，都是一場財富大洗牌。日本升息宣告了舊套利模式的終結，而人民幣的承壓則凸顯了中國經濟內部難解的結構困局。
但對於身處科技主升段的台股投資人來說，切莫被跨國套利的雜訊嚇破膽。正如吳嘉隆所言，貨幣的遷徙只是河流的轉向，並不會阻擋 AI 與科技革命的大海奔騰。
看清「套利平倉不等於股市崩盤」的總經真相，在市場藉由國際匯市波動下殺洗盤時，堅定逢低布局具備全球核心競爭力的科技龍頭（如跌破 2,400 元的台積電）與剛需受惠族群（如資訊安全），才能在這場跨國資本大亂鬥中，穩坐釣魚台、笑納長線暴利！

paras_en: Global financial markets' sensitive nerves were once again sharply jolted by abnormal moves in East Asia's two major currencies.

On one side, the Bank of Japan, which has maintained an ultra‑easy monetary policy for years, started raising rates in September and the market broadly expects another move in December, possibly pushing the policy rate toward the 2% mark; on the other side, global hedge funds and cross‑border arbitrageurs are quietly shifting their borrowing target to the next ultra‑low‑rate currency – the Chinese renminbi (RMB).

"Will the yen’s rate hike trigger a global carry‑trade unwind? Will the stock market collapse because of it?" Faced with investors’ flood of anxiety, macro‑economics guru Wu Jialong bluntly shattered the market myth on the show "What Stock Investors Want to Know": "Unwinding arbitrage trades is inevitable, but the stock market will definitely not crash – don’t force these two things together! The real headache isn’t the global equity market, it’s the People’s Bank of China whose foreign‑exchange reserves are about to face a severe test!"

1. Breaking the Zero‑Rate Myth! Why does the BOJ "have to" raise rates above 2%? Over the past decades, the most classic "risk‑free money‑machine" for global investors has been to tap Japan’s near‑zero‑cost funds, borrow yen in huge amounts from the Bank of Japan, and funnel them abroad to buy high‑yielding U.S. Treasuries, U.S. stocks or tech‑giant equities. That massive arbitrage game is now being ended by the BOJ itself.
Wu Jialong points out that the BOJ’s rate hike this time is "inevitable and unavoidable":

Import‑driven inflation out of control: Japan’s once‑proud deflation has long vanished; current inflation has been staying above 2.5‑3% for years and even neared 4% at times. If the policy rate stays below 1%, real negative rates will continue to erode domestic purchasing power.

Pure exchange‑rate intervention is ineffective: The huge yield gap between the U.S. and Japan leaves the yen on a long‑term path of destructive depreciation. Past attempts by the Japanese government to defend the yen by selling U.S. Treasuries and deploying dollar cash proved to be a drop in the bucket. "The only solution is for Japan’s rate hikes to catch up with or even exceed the U.S., thereby narrowing the U.S.–Japan yield spread!"

"Rates must move above 2%. It sounds extreme for a country accustomed to zero rates, but only a stronger yen can make import prices cheaper and fully alleviate Japan’s import‑driven inflation, creating a virtuous economic cycle," Wu analyzes.

2. Global Unwinding Wave Emerging! Wu Jialong: Stock‑Market Crash? You’re Overthinking It! As the BOJ steadfastly walks the rate‑hike path, the international arbitrage army has no choice but to launch a massive debt clean‑up:
Investors must sell their high‑yielding dollar assets;
Convert the proceeds back into yen;
Send the yen home to repay the original yen loans.
This process indeed brings “capital flowing back to Japan and pushing the yen higher,” but the market‑driven panic that follows is: “If capital flees dollar assets, will global equities crash?”
"Absolutely not!" Wu Jialong sharply rebuts this over‑hyped fear:

"Arbitrage unwind is merely the deleveraging of a portion of highly leveraged speculative capital. The long‑term trajectory of equities ultimately depends on corporate fundamentals and the real profits generated by technological revolutions. Equating a capital‑structure adjustment with a stock‑market crash is simply overthinking!"

Wu emphasizes that the current pull‑back in equities is essentially to digest valuations and rotate holdings; the massive AI‑industry orders and long‑term demand have not disappeared, so a systemic crash cannot be caused solely by a yen‑carry‑trade unwind.

3. The Next Target to Be Borrowed‑Up: The Renminbi Becomes the "New Money‑Machine" When yen borrowing costs rise and are no longer cheap, the huge pool of cross‑border arbitrage capital instantly shifts its radar to the next ultra‑low‑rate currency basin – the renminbi.
Wu lists a shocking comparison of 10‑year sovereign yields worldwide:
China 10‑year sovereign yield: about 1.68%;
Japan 10‑year sovereign yield: about 3.0%;
U.S. 10‑year sovereign yield: about 5.2%;

"Look how tempting that spread is!" Wu reveals the arbitrage calculations of large international banks and financial institutions: Because of China’s real‑estate bubble and weak real economy, large state‑owned banks are flush with idle funds. For arbitrageurs, borrowing RMB domestically costs less than 2%, converting it to dollars and investing in U.S. Treasuries instantly yields a solid return of over 5%!
This risk‑free spread of more than three percentage points quickly lets the renminbi replace the yen as the core player in the next round of global arbitrage trades.

4. The PBOC’s Nightmare: FX Reserves Under Strain and a "Policy Dilemma" The currency shift in arbitrage may be a minor tweak for global equities, but for the People’s Bank of China it is a lethal financial storm.
Wu dissects the standard RMB‑arbitrage flow: borrow RMB in China ➔ exchange with the PBOC for dollars ➔ remit the dollars abroad for investment.
This creates two devastating chain reactions for China:

Foreign‑exchange reserves face severe depletion: massive capital legally exits China through the arbitrage channel, effectively moving the PBOC’s precious dollar reserves out day by day. Once reserves fall below a safety threshold, China’s ability to defend the exchange rate and import essential goods will be seriously weakened.
Caught in an inescapable monetary‑policy dilemma:
If rates are cut to rescue the real economy: the domestic yield gap widens further, accelerating capital outflows and triggering a cliff‑fall depreciation of the renminbi;
If rates are raised to stop capital flight: the already suffocating Chinese real‑estate sector and domestic manufacturing will collapse under the pressure of higher financing costs!

"A weak real economy should, in theory, call for rate cuts and a weaker currency to boost exports; but massive capital outflows squeeze FX reserves, forcing you to raise rates to defend the currency. China’s monetary policy will soon be trapped in an excruciating contradiction, and ultimately may have to resort to harsher ‘iron‑fist capital controls’ to seal the leak!"

Conclusion: Understand the Massive Capital Migration, Position Long‑Term Without Panic Every policy shift in the financial markets reshuffles wealth on a grand scale. Japan’s rate hike signals the end of the old arbitrage model, while pressure on the renminbi highlights China’s deep‑seated structural challenges.

But for Taiwan‑stock investors riding the tech‑driven rally, don’t let cross‑border arbitrage noise scare you. As Wu says, currency migration is merely a river changing course; it won’t stop the tidal surge of AI and the tech revolution.

Seeing the macro truth that “arbitrage unwind does not equal a stock‑market crash,” when markets are shaken by international FX volatility, firmly build positions in globally competitive tech leaders (e.g., TSMC if it falls below NT$2,400) and essential beneficiaries (e.g., cybersecurity firms) to sit on the high ground and capture long‑term profits in this cross‑border capital melee!

items.title_en: AI Compute Giant's Bond Yield Soars 15%! Credit Crisis About to Explode? Tech Stock Pullback a Bubble? Wu Jialong: Copy Amazon of Its Day! Switch Hands and Grab This Group!
paras: 近期全球金融市場被一則震撼彈打破平靜：指標型 AI 算力租賃獨角獸 CoreWeave，其發行的無擔保公司債殖利率竟然一路飆破 15%！
這項驚人數據瞬間引爆華爾街的避險神經。部分對沖基金開始高呼「拋售 AI 公司債、轉買美國公債」，市場更充斥著「科技巨頭資本支出過大、自由現金流轉負、AI 恐引爆新一輪企業違約信貸危機」的恐慌言論。連帶地，美股科技股重挫、台股跌破半年線，散戶人人自危：「AI 的牛市神話真的要破滅了嗎？」
對此，知名總經大師吳嘉隆在《股民想知道》節目中給出全然不同的逆向思維，一針見血地指出：「市場最不缺的就是藉題發揮的鬼故事！這根本不是什麼系統性信貸危機，而是大行情在暴衝後必然發生的『洗籌碼換手』！這場景，跟當年網路革命時期的亞馬遜（Amazon）如出一轍！」

一、解密 15% 殖利率真相：個別槓桿過大，被誇大成「系統危機」
為什麼 CoreWeave 的公司債殖利率會飆到 15% 的高利貸水準？市場是不是真的要爆發連鎖違約？
吳嘉隆深入拆解其財務結構，點出市場「以偏概全」的盲點：
單一公司的極端槓桿： CoreWeave 是一家專門採購輝達 GPU、提供算力雲端租賃的新創公司。它的問題在於財務槓桿開得過大，且本身缺乏實體不動產作為發債擔保品，屬於純粹的信用貸款，風險溢價自然偏高。
(圖片來源:優分析產業資料庫)
同業並未出現連鎖反應： 反觀從事相同算力租賃業務的同業，如 IREN 或 Nebius，其發行的債券殖利率並未出現失控飆升的現象。換言之，這完全是一個「個別企業財務操作」的個案，絕非整個 AI 產業鏈的系統性危機！
軍火庫巨頭的全力奧援： CoreWeave 背後站著大股東兼關鍵晶片供應商——輝達（NVIDIA）。在算力依然供不應求的大環境下，只要輝達介入協調資源，這家算力要角根本不可能輕易倒下。
「華爾街只是藉著這個理由，製造恐慌情緒來大舉打壓股價、藉機調節風險資產，」吳嘉隆直言，投資人千萬別把機構法人的「洗盤藉口」當成世界末日。

二、產業革命的必然規律：技術疑慮與融資疑慮
回顧人類歷史上每一次顛覆性的科技革命，從蒸汽機、鐵路、個人電腦到網際網路，無一例外都會經歷兩大質疑：「技術疑慮」與「融資疑慮」。
融資疑慮： 「大家借了這麼多錢蓋資料中心，最後到底能不能賺到錢？會不會還不出利息？」
技術疑慮： 「Google 研發的 TPU 好像不需要那麼多高階記憶體？新晶片架構會不會推翻原來的零組件需求？」
吳嘉隆指出，這種懷疑非常正常，因為科技革命永遠遵循著**「供給端先行、需求端後至」**的規律：「現在各大雲端巨頭瘋狂擴建算力，屬於基礎設施的『供給端』鋪設。這個時候，很多終端應用與變現模式『根本還沒被發明出來』！」
就像 1990 年代鋪設全球光纖網路時，沒人能預見未來的 YouTube 串流影音、智慧型手機行動支付與 Uber 外送平台一樣。現在大家只看到 AI 能寫稿、畫圖、剪影片，但未來的具身智能機器人、智慧醫療新藥研發、自動駕駛全路網調度，將會源源不絕地創造出當前難以想像的百倍算力需求！

三、複製當年亞馬遜：從「連年虧損」到「市值前五」的奇蹟
面對當前市場對「AI 企業何時能轉虧為盈」的質疑，吳嘉隆直接搬出當年的經典教材——亞馬遜（Amazon）。
在 2000 年網路泡沫破滅前後，亞馬遜是一家被華爾街天天唱衰「遲早破產」的公司。它不僅連年大幅虧損，自由現金流慘不忍睹，股價更是慘跌超過 90%。但亞馬遜究竟是怎麼撐過那段黑暗歲月、最終成為市值數兆美元的龐大帝國？
「因為它在打底的過程中，不斷利用現有的基礎設施，瘋狂開拓全新的業務！」
從一開始純粹在網路上「賣書」；
到後來跨足「賣 CD 音樂、賣生活百貨」；
再到打造全美最大的線上電商市集；
最終，它將內部多餘的運算架構商業化，開創了改變全球科技版圖的**「AWS 雲端運算服務」**！
吳嘉隆強調，現在的 AI 算力服務商走的就是這條路。短期內看似在「燒錢搞基建」，但隨著周邊輔助技術的成熟，新的商業模式會迅速被創造出來。時間會證明，許多優質 AI 企業的真實營收與獲利，將遠遠超出市場最樂觀的預期。

四、換手整理再攻！大跌時「抱緊這兩大族群」
既然 AI 的多頭趨勢堅不可摧，為什麼近期台美股會出現如此劇烈的回檔？
答案正是：「建立新共識，籌碼大換手！」
吳嘉隆一針見血地分析：「行情漲到一定位階，低檔進場的人（例如台積電買在 1,800～1,900 元的人）獲利豐厚，隨時想落袋為安。此時市場必須藉由『信貸危機、中東開戰』等理由砸盤修正，讓這些短線浮額退場，引進成本在 2,300～2,400 元的新資金。這些新進場的人不會急著賣，籌碼沉澱後，大盤才有基礎再度向 5 萬點發動總攻！」
在這場波瀾壯闊的換手大戲中，投資人究竟該抱緊哪些族群？吳嘉隆給出兩大明確方向：

1. 護國神山「台積電」（2330）：跌下來是送分題！
全球正在興建與規劃中的台積電新廠超過 20 座，這代表終端巨頭的需求不是虛火，而是實打實的產能飢渴。「台積電拉回跌破 2,400 元、回測 2,300 元，有閒錢的人就該加減買起來放！它終究要跨過 2,600 元再刷歷史新高！」
(圖片來源:優分析產業資料庫)

2. 美中防駭新剛需：「資訊安全概念股」！
AI 算力鋪得越龐大，駭客利用高階 AI 破壞基礎設施的風險就越高。美國與台灣已將「資安」提升至國家安全層級，成為絕對不能縮減的剛性支出。近期當硬體零組件劇烈修正時，本土資安族群卻逆勢飆升，顯示聰明的主力資金早已悄悄轉進這個低基期、高毛利的避風港！

結語：恐慌是散戶的毒藥，卻是贏家的蜜糖
投資市場永遠循環著一句真理：「在絕望中誕生，在半信半疑中成長，在憧憬中成熟，在希望中破滅。」
面對 15% 債券殖利率的聳動標題，盲目跟風停損只會讓你砍在景氣循環的阿呆谷。看懂當年亞馬遜的涅槃重生，讀懂主力洗籌碼的背後陽謀，趁著這波換手拉回的黃金時刻，抱緊台積電與資安黑馬，你就是下一波行情噴發時的最大贏家！

paras_en: Recently, the global financial markets were shaken by a bombshell: the benchmark AI compute‑rental unicorn CoreWeave saw the yield on its unsecured corporate bonds surge past 15%!

The startling figure instantly triggered Wall Street's hedging nerves. Some hedge funds began shouting "sell AI corporate bonds, buy US Treasuries," and the market was flooded with panic talk about "tech giants' capital expenditures being too large, free cash flow turning negative, AI fears sparking a new wave of corporate default credit crises." Consequently, US tech stocks slumped, Taiwan's market fell below its six‑month line, and retail investors grew anxious: "Is the AI bull‑market myth finally collapsing?"

In response, well‑known macro‑economist Wu Jialong offered a completely opposite contrarian view on the show "What Investors Want to Know," sharply pointing out: "What the market lacks most are ghost stories spun from the headline! This is not a systemic credit crisis at all, but a 'chip‑turnover' that inevitably follows a big rally's surge. The scene is just like Amazon during the internet‑revolution era!"

1. Unmasking the 15% Yield: an Isolated Leverage Issue Exaggerated into a "Systemic Crisis" Why did CoreWeave's corporate‑bond yield climb to a usurious 15% level? Is the market really on the brink of a cascade of defaults?
Wu Jialong dissected the company's financial structure and highlighted the market's "hasty generalization" flaw:

CoreWeave is a startup that purchases NVIDIA GPUs and provides cloud compute rentals. Its problem lies in excessive financial leverage and the lack of real‑estate collateral, making it a pure credit loan with naturally high risk premium.
(Image source: You Analysis Industry Database)

No chain reaction among peers: By contrast, peers in the same compute‑rental business such as IREN or Nebius have not seen their bond yields spiral out of control. In other words, this is purely an "individual corporate financial operation" case, not a systemic crisis across the AI industry chain!

Full‑throttle backing from a weapons‑grade player: Behind CoreWeave stands a major shareholder and key chip supplier—NVIDIA. In an environment where compute capacity remains in short supply, as long as NVIDIA steps in to coordinate resources, this compute heavyweight cannot easily collapse.

"Wall Street is merely using this as a pretext to create panic, crush stock prices and adjust risk assets," Wu said, warning investors not to treat institutional "chip‑turnover" excuses as the end of the world.

2. Inevitable Law of Industry Revolutions: Technical and Financing Concerns Looking back at every disruptive technological revolution in human history—from the steam engine, railroads, personal computers to the internet—each has invariably faced two major doubts: "technical concerns" and "financing concerns."
Financing concern: "Everyone borrowed so much money to build data centers; in the end, will they actually make money? Can they even pay the interest?"
Technical concern: "Google's TPU seems to need less high‑end memory; will new chip architectures overturn existing component demand?"

Wu noted that such skepticism is normal because tech revolutions always follow the rule of **"supply leads, demand follows"**: "Now the major cloud giants are frantically expanding compute capacity, which is the infrastructure 'supply side.' At this stage, many end‑user applications and monetization models have literally not been invented yet!"

Just as in the 1990s when the global fiber‑optic network was being laid and no one could foresee YouTube streaming, smartphones, mobile payments or Uber, today we only see AI writing articles, drawing pictures, editing videos, but future embodied intelligent robots, smart‑medical drug development, and autonomous‑driving network dispatch will continuously generate unimaginable hundred‑fold compute demand!

3. Copying Amazon’s Path: From "Years of Losses" to "Top‑Five Market‑Cap" Miracle Facing current market doubts about "when AI firms will turn profitable," Wu directly brought up the classic case study—Amazon.

Before and after the 2000 dot‑com bust, Amazon was a company Wall Street sang about daily, predicting "it will go bankrupt sooner or later." It suffered consecutive massive losses, abysmal free cash flow, and its stock plunged more than 90%. Yet how did Amazon survive that dark period and eventually become a multi‑trillion‑dollar empire?
"Because during its foundation phase it constantly leveraged existing infrastructure to wildly expand into brand‑new businesses!"
It started by simply selling books online;
then expanded to selling CDs and general merchandise;
later built the largest online retail marketplace in the United States;
and finally commercialized its excess computing infrastructure, creating the globally transformative **"AWS cloud computing service"**!

Wu emphasized that today's AI compute providers are walking the same path. In the short term they appear to be "burning cash on infrastructure," but as surrounding technologies mature, new business models will be created rapidly. Time will prove that many quality AI firms' real revenues and profits will far exceed the market's most optimistic expectations.

4. Switch‑Hands Re‑Organization and Attack! Hold Tight to These Two Sectors During a Crash Since AI’s bullish trend is unshakable, why have US and Taiwan markets recently suffered such sharp pullbacks?
The answer is: "Establish a new consensus, massive chip turnover!"

Wu cut to the chase: "When a rally reaches a certain level, low‑price entrants (e.g., those who bought TSMC at NT$1,800‑1,900) enjoy hefty profits and are ready to lock them in. At that moment the market must use reasons like ‘credit crisis’ or ‘Middle‑East conflict’ to trigger a correction, flushing out these short‑term gains and bringing in new capital at NT$2,300‑2,400. These newcomers won’t rush to sell; after the chips settle, the market gains a solid base to launch another push toward the 50,000‑point mark!"
In this grand turnover drama, which groups should investors cling to? Wu gave two clear directions:

1. The national treasure "TSMC" (2330): a dip is a free‑point giveaway! Over 20 new TSMC fabs are being built or planned worldwide, indicating that demand from end‑users is real and hungry for capacity. "When TSMC slides below NT$2,400 and tests NT$2,300, those with cash should buy in and hold! It will eventually break past NT$2,600 and set new highs!"
(Image source: You Analysis Industry Database)

2. The new US‑China cyber‑defense necessity: "Information‑security concept stocks"! The larger the AI compute footprint, the higher the risk of hackers using advanced AI to sabotage infrastructure. The US and Taiwan have elevated "cybersecurity" to a national‑security level, making it an inflexible, non‑cuttable expense. Recently, when hardware component stocks sharply corrected, domestic cybersecurity stocks surged against the tide, showing that savvy capital has already quietly shifted into this low‑base, high‑margin safe haven!

Conclusion: Panic is a poison for retail investors but honey for winners The investment market always cycles around a truth: "Born in despair, grown in doubt, matured in aspiration, and shattered in hope."

Facing the eye‑popping 15% bond‑yield headline, blindly following the crowd to cut losses will only land you in the “dumb‑valley” of the business cycle. Understand Amazon’s phoenix rebirth, read the hidden motives behind institutional chip‑turnover, and during this golden turnover pull‑back, cling to TSMC and the cybersecurity dark horse—you’ll be the biggest winner when the next wave erupts!

items.title: 聯發科延攬前英特爾執行副總裁 擴大資料中心與AI布局
items.title_en: MediaTek Recruits Former Intel Executive Vice President to Expand Data Center and AI Portfolio
paras: IC設計大廠聯發科(2454-TW)積極擴大資料中心與AI布局，再度延攬半導體重量級人才，今(4)日宣布，前英特爾(Intel)(INTC-US)執行副總裁Navid Shahriari，將於11月9日加入公司擔任資深副總經理，未來將負責先進製程、良率平台、設計技術協同優化(DTCO)、先進測試與封裝，以及品質暨可靠性團隊。
據了解，Navid Shahriari在英特爾任職長達37年，歷任工程及技術管理職務，曾擔任英特爾執行副總裁，負責製造與產品工程及先進封裝相關業務，並具備資料中心產品開發經驗。其專業涵蓋半導體製造、晶片設計、先進封裝、測試及量產管理，熟悉EMIB、Foveros等異質整合技術。
聯發科指出，Navid Shahriari直接向總經理暨營運長報告，核心任務之一是依據公司未來發展策略，深化與台積電(2330-TW)等重要供應鏈夥伴的合作，透過先進技術的協同開發與整合，持續提升產品競爭力，協助公司提供具市場競爭力的AI與高速運算產品。
paras_en: MediaTek (2454-TW), a major IC design company, is actively expanding its data center and AI footprint and has once again recruited a heavyweight semiconductor talent. Today (the 4th), it announced that former Intel (INTC-US) Executive Vice President Navid Shahriari will join the company on November 9 as Senior Vice General Manager, responsible for advanced processes, yield platforms, design‑technology co‑optimization (DTCO), advanced testing and packaging, as well as quality and reliability teams.

Shahriari spent 37 years at Intel, holding various engineering and technology management roles. He previously served as Intel’s Executive Vice President overseeing manufacturing, product engineering, and advanced packaging businesses, and has experience developing data‑center products. His expertise spans semiconductor manufacturing, chip design, advanced packaging, testing and mass‑production management, and he is familiar with heterogeneous integration technologies such as EMIB and Foveros.

MediaTek noted that Shahriari will report directly to the General Manager and COO. One of his core missions is to deepen collaboration with key supply‑chain partners such as TSMC (2330‑TW) in line with the company’s future development strategy, leveraging joint development and integration of advanced technologies to continuously enhance product competitiveness and help the company deliver market‑leading AI and high‑speed computing products.

items.title: 不只台積電！AI搞越大越缺「它」！美中角力新戰場！吳嘉隆點名「這族群」主力悄悄卡位：防駭客成剛需大贏家！
items.title_en: Not Just TSMC! AI’s Growth Increases Demand for Cybersecurity – The New US‑China Battleground, Says Wu Chia‑Long, Who Highlights This Sector as a Quietly Positioned Dark Horse
paras: 當全球科技巨頭為了爭奪通用人工智慧（AGI）的聖杯，瘋狂砸下數千億美元採購晶片、擴建伺服器時，市場的目光大多聚焦在台積電、輝達（NVIDIA）等硬體代工與算力軍火商身上。然而，許多投資人忽視了一個致命的問題——如果最強大的 AI 基礎設施，最終淪為黑客與敵對勢力的作案工具，這場科技革命將演變成一場全球災難！
在台股回測半年線、外資大舉調節的震盪行情中，總經大師吳嘉隆在《股民想知道》節目中語出驚人地指出：「資訊安全沒有做好，拼命搞 AI 其實是極其糟糕的！AI 搞得越龐大，市場就越缺『防駭客技術』，這已經成為美中角力的新戰場，也是主力資金正在暗中卡位的下一匹黑馬！」

一、AI 的雙面刃：算力越強，安全漏洞越致命
過去兩年，市場對 AI 的想像多半停留在「提高生產力」：寫程式、生影片、做行銷、或是驅動無人自駕與機器人。但吳嘉隆提醒，科技是一把鋒利的雙面刃，伴隨著龐大算力誕生的，是新型態的犯罪與國家安全威脅。
「現在大家看到很多電信詐騙、深度偽造（Deepfake），背後全是用 AI 技術在支撐；更嚴重的是，駭客利用高階算力破解防禦系統，已經開始侵入各國的關鍵基礎設施！」
吳嘉隆透露，美國情報與國防機構近期高度戒備，發現來自中國的頂級駭客組織，正利用先進的 AI 滲透技術，悄悄入侵美國的電信網路、能源電網甚至是軍事供應鏈的電腦系統。「如果我們花費天文數字建置好的資料中心與算力模型，反過來被敵對陣營或犯罪集團拿去搞破壞，那不是天下大亂嗎？」
這也解釋了為什麼近期國際科技巨頭在瘋狂推進 AI 的同時，不得不稍微放慢腳步——因為在享受算力紅利之前，必須先補齊「資訊安全（Cybersecurity）」這道最核心的防火牆！

二、美中博弈新戰場：從晶片封鎖到「資安防線」
美中科技戰的本質，早已從單純的「晶片禁令」升級至「系統與數據防衛戰」。
吳嘉隆深入分析，美國前總統川普若在此次期中選舉後繼續推動其國家戰略，應對中國的挑戰絕對是重中之重。除了防堵先進晶片流入中國，另一個關鍵戰場就是全面清除潛藏在盟國供應鏈中的資訊安全隱患。
不可替代的「剛性需求」：記憶體、被動元件或銅箔基板（CCL）會受到景氣循環與原物料成本的波動影響，但「防駭客與資訊安全」屬於絕對不能被刪減的剛性支出。企業或政府可以延後更換硬體，卻絕不能冒著被駭客癱瘓系統、勒索鉅款的風險。
法規硬指標的全面推動：隨著美國五角大廈與國土安全部針對國防供應鏈推行嚴格的資安成熟度認證（CMMC），任何想要吃到歐美 AI 供應鏈大單的台廠，資安防禦能力已經從「加分題」變成了「入場券」。
這項政策與地緣戰略的推進，直接為資訊安全產業注入了長達數年的長線成長動能。

三、盤面悄悄換手！主力資金為何相中「資安族群」？
觀察近期台股的盤面結構，可以發現一個極具啟發性的現象：當記憶體、載板等先前漲多的硬體股因估值過高而劇烈回檔時，台灣本土的資訊安全族群卻逆勢走出獨立多頭行情，股價表現相當強勢。
吳嘉隆點破主力資金的思維邏輯：
「很多人只盯著硬體題材漲價，但主力看的是產業革命的下一階段。資訊安全現在全面上來，就是因為大資金已經意識到這件事的嚴重性與爆發力！」
與傳統硬體製造業相比，資安族群具備三大獨特優勢：
不受原物料暴漲侵蝕毛利： 資安以軟體、韌體、雲端防禦架構為核心，不會像硬體組裝廠面臨「銅箔、玻纖布漲價吃掉利潤」的窘境，普遍維持 40%～60% 以上的高毛利率。
高續約率的訂閱制現金流： 企業一旦導入一套資安系統，轉換成本極高，每年穩定的維護費與軟體授權，為公司帶來穩健的自由現金流。
台灣戰略地位的特殊性： 台灣地處全球地緣政治與網路攻擊的最前線，每天面臨數百萬次的境外駭客侵擾，使得台灣本土資安業者練就了極強的實戰防禦經驗，在全球供應鏈中具備極高性價比。

四、投資人的攻守平衡策略：台積電為盾，資安股為矛
面對大盤跌破半年線、洗盤整理的震盪階段，投資人究竟該如何配置資金，才能安穩度過波動、並在下一波攻勢中大獲全勝？
吳嘉隆建議採取**「雙核心戰略」**：
核心防守（逢低布局台積電）：台積電全球擴產超過 20 座新廠，訂單能見度直達先進製程的最前端。股價若因大盤修正回測 2,400 元甚至 2,300 元，「有閒錢就加減買一點起來放」，這檔龍頭股終究要跨越 2,600 元再創新高，是資產防禦的基石。
(圖片來源:優分析產業資料庫)
爆發攻擊（鎖定低基期的資安黑馬）：在硬體零組件本益比偏高的當下，將目光轉向基期相對偏低、受惠於美中資安角力與企業剛需的資訊安全概念股。跟隨主力資金換手的腳步，在整理區間分批卡位，享受 AI 應用落地時最純粹的軟體紅利。

結語：淘金熱的時代，別忘了替金庫加把鎖！
19 世紀加州淘金熱時，最賺錢的往往不是淘金客，而是賣牛仔褲與鐵鍬的人；而在 21 世紀的這場 AI 算力淘金狂潮中，台積電打造了最強大的鐵鍬，而資訊安全產業，則是每一位淘金者都必須花大錢僱用的保鏢與金庫守衛！
當市場還在為短期的地緣政治與升息雜音恐慌時，看懂「AI 越發達，防駭越剛需」的底層邏輯，提前與主力一同卡位資安族群，你將在這波科技換手的浪潮中，抓住下一個翻倍大贏家的歷史機遇！

paras_en: As global tech giants pour trillions of dollars into chips and server farms to chase the holy grail of artificial general intelligence (AGI), market attention has largely centered on hardware makers like TSMC and NVIDIA. Yet many investors overlook a fatal flaw—if the most powerful AI infrastructure ends up as a tool for hackers and hostile actors, the tech revolution could turn into a worldwide disaster.

During a volatile Taiwanese market phase marked by a half‑year moving‑average test and heavy foreign‑investor rebalancing, macro‑economist Wu Chia‑Long shocked listeners on the “Investors Want to Know” program: “If information security is not solid, pushing AI at all costs is disastrous. The larger AI becomes, the more the market lacks ‘anti‑hacking technology.’ This is now the new front in the US‑China rivalry and the next dark‑horse that big money is quietly positioning for.”

1. AI’s Double‑Edged Sword: More Compute, More Critical Vulnerabilities. Over the past two years, most AI hype focused on productivity gains—coding, video creation, marketing, autonomous driving, robotics. Wu warns that technology is a sharp double‑edged sword; massive compute power also spawns new crimes and national‑security threats.

“Today we see a surge in telecom scams and deepfakes, all powered by AI. Even worse, hackers are using high‑end compute to crack defenses and have already begun infiltrating critical infrastructure worldwide.”

Wu disclosed that U.S. intelligence and defense agencies are on high alert after detecting top‑tier Chinese hacker groups employing advanced AI‑driven intrusion techniques to silently breach U.S. telecom networks, power grids, and even military supply‑chain computer systems. “If we spend astronomical sums building data centers and compute models only to have adversaries turn them against us, isn’t that a recipe for global chaos?”

This explains why major international tech firms, while racing ahead with AI, are now forced to slow down slightly—because before reaping compute benefits, they must first shore up the core firewall of cybersecurity.
2. The New US‑China Battleground: From Chip Embargoes to “Cyber‑Defense Lines.” The essence of the tech war has shifted from simple chip bans to a broader system‑and‑data defense conflict.

Wu’s deep dive notes that if former President Trump continues his national‑strategic agenda after the upcoming mid‑term elections, countering China will be a top priority. Beyond blocking advanced chips from reaching China, a key front is eradicating hidden cybersecurity risks within allied supply chains.

An “inelastic demand” item: while memory, passive components, or copper‑clad laminates (CCL) swing with economic cycles and raw‑material costs, “anti‑hacking and information security” is a non‑negotiable, rigid expense. Companies or governments can postpone hardware upgrades, but they cannot risk system paralysis or massive ransomware payouts.

Regulatory push: With the U.S. Pentagon and Department of Homeland Security enforcing strict cybersecurity maturity certifications (CMMC) for defense supply chains, any Taiwanese supplier eyeing large European‑American AI contracts now needs cybersecurity capability not as a bonus but as an entry ticket.
These policies, combined with geopolitical strategy, inject multi‑year growth momentum into the cybersecurity industry.

3. Market Rotation in Silence: Why Big Money Is Targeting the “Cybersecurity Group.” A look at recent Taiwanese market structure reveals a striking pattern: when hardware stocks like memory and substrates tumble after overvaluation, domestic cybersecurity stocks defy the trend, posting strong bullish moves.
Wu breaks down the logic of institutional investors:

“Many only watch hardware price spikes, but the smart money is focused on the next phase of the industry revolution. Cybersecurity is booming now because large capital has recognized its seriousness and explosive potential.”
Compared with traditional hardware manufacturers, the cybersecurity sector enjoys three distinct advantages:

No raw‑material cost erosion: Cybersecurity revolves around software, firmware, and cloud‑based defense architectures, avoiding profit‑squeezing issues like rising copper‑foil or fiberglass prices, and typically maintains gross margins of 40‑60% or higher.
High‑renewal subscription cash flow: Once a firm adopts a security solution, switching costs are huge; recurring maintenance fees and software licenses generate stable free‑cash‑flow streams.

Taiwan’s strategic position: Situated at the front line of global geopolitics and cyber attacks, Taiwan faces millions of foreign intrusion attempts daily. This gives local security firms unparalleled real‑world defense experience and a superior cost‑performance edge in the global supply chain.

4. Investor Playbook: TSMC as Shield, Cybersecurity Stocks as Spear. With the market below its half‑year moving average and undergoing a shake‑out, how should investors allocate capital to weather volatility and win the next wave?
Wu recommends a “dual‑core strategy”:

Defensive core (buy TSMC on dips): TSMC is expanding with more than 20 new fabs worldwide, with order visibility deep into advanced nodes. If the stock retests 2,400 or even 2,300 TWD, “add a little on the dip”—the leader must break past 2,600 TWD for new highs and serves as a defensive asset foundation.
(Image source: You Analysis Industry Database)

Aggressive thrust (target low‑base cybersecurity dark horses): With hardware component P/E ratios stretched, shift focus to lower‑base, cybersecurity concepts that benefit from US‑China cyber rivalry and corporate necessity. Follow the institutional rotation, accumulate in the consolidation zone, and capture pure software upside as AI applications materialize.

Conclusion: In a gold‑rush era, remember to lock the vault. In the 19th‑century California gold rush, the biggest earners sold jeans and shovels, not the miners. In today’s AI compute gold rush, TSMC builds the ultimate shovel, while the cybersecurity industry provides the bodyguards and vault locks every prospector must hire.

When the market is still jittery over short‑term geopolitical and rate‑hike noise, understanding the underlying logic that “the more advanced AI gets, the greater the need for anti‑hacking” lets you position alongside the main players in the cybersecurity sector and seize the next double‑up opportunity in this tech turnover wave.
